old_digest: The match, when not played out, shall be decided by the first innings.
new_digest: The match, unless played out, shall be decided by the first innings.

old_digest: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consists of 5 or 6 balls.
new_digest: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consist of 5 or 6 balls.

old_digest: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consists of 5 or 6 balls.
One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards.
new_digest: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of twenty-two yards.

old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed twentytwo yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side neither byes, leg-byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped. xi.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither byes, leg-byes, nor other throws shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.

old_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease and turn before the ball cross the ground to entitle him to another.
new_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease, and turn before the bail cross the ground to entitle him to another.

old_digest: A match is played between two sides of eleven players each, unless otherwise agreed to; each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 54.
new_digest: A match is played between two sides of eleven players each, unless otherwise agreed to; each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 53.

old_digest: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call “No ball.” iii.
new_digest: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call "No-ball.”

old_digest: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “No-Ball.”
new_digest: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call "No ball.”

old_digest: The ball shall be bowled in overs of four balls from each wicket alternately. When four balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “Over.” Neither a “No-ball” nor a “Wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the
new_digest: The ball shall be bowled in overs of five balls from each wicket alternately. When five balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call "Over." Neither a "No-ball" nor a "Wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over."

old_digest: The bowler may not change ends more than twice in the same innings nor bowl more than two overs in succession.
new_digest: The bowler shall be allowed to change ends as often as he pleases, provided only that he does not bowl two overs consecutively in one innings.

old_digest: The striker may hit a “no-ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no-ball,” unless he be run out or break laws 26, 27, 29, 30.
new_digest: The striker may hit a "no ball," and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a "noball,” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29, 30.

old_digest: If the ball, not having been called “ wide ” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “bye;” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “ leg-byes” respectively.
new_digest: If the ball, not having been called "wide" or "no ball," pass the striker, without touching his bat or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call "Bye,” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted), and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call "Leg bye,” such runs to be scored "byes” and "leg byes” respectively.

old_digest: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—“Caught.” v.
new_digest: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—

old_digest: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with the hand or arm, with ball in hand:—“Stumped.”
new_digest: Or, if in playing at the ball, providing it be not touched by the bat or hand, the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with the hand or arm, with ball in hand:—

old_digest: Or, if the ball be struck, or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands:—“Hit the ball twice.”
new_digest: Or, if the ball be struck, or be struck by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.”

old_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead;” but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No-Ball.”
new_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled, in the wicketkeeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead,” but when the bowler, is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out, but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result it shall be scored “No ball.”

old_digest: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.
new_digest: The ball shall weigh no less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.

old_digest: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise the ball shall be “ dead,” and five runs added to the score. Whatever runs may have been made five only shall be added.
new_digest: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise, the ball shall be dead, and five runs added to the score; whatever runs may have been made, five only shall be added.

old_digest: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No-ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
new_digest: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_digest: No umpire shall be changed during a match unless with the consent of both sides, except in case of violation of Law 52, then either side may dismiss him.
new_digest: No umpire shall be changed during a match unless with the consent of both sides, except in case of violation of Law 51, then either side may dismiss him.
On the last day of a match and in a one day match at any time, the in-side may declare their innings at any end.

old_digest: The bails shall be each 4¾in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_digest: The bails shall be each 4½in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.

old_digest: This shall not prevent the batsman from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman nor bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.
new_digest: This shall not prevent the batsmen from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman or bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.
